name: I See Dead People
look: A close-up still from The Sixth Sense: Haley Joel Osment as young Cole lies in bed with a pink knit blanket pulled up to his chin, eyes wet and wide with fear as he whispers to someone.
use: A spin on the film's line "I see dead people." The caption swaps in something the speaker keeps noticing everywhere, like typos, dying houseplants or abandoned projects, delivered in the kid's scared whisper.
examples: Me walking into my apartment after a two-week vacation
Me opening the shared office fridge
describe: scared little boy in bed whispering a secret
haley joel osment teary eyed under a pink blanket
kid from the ghost movie saying he sees ghosts
frightened child tucked into bed looking up
boy with watery eyes confessing something creepy
origin: From M. Night Shyamalan's 1999 film The Sixth Sense, where Cole (Haley Joel Osment) whispers "I see dead people" to his psychologist.
